question: What if your product photo could spin around — in full 3D?

hook_visual.intent: three fabricated product photos that read as spinnable 3D objects

points.claim: idol turns a single picture of an object into a full three-D Gaussian splat, including the sides the picture never showed.
points.spoken: idol turns one single picture into a full three-D Gaussian splat, even the sides your camera never saw.
points.source_note: Model card: 'Idol turns one picture of an object into a 3D Gaussian splat… including the sides the picture never showed.'

visual.intent: one photo, then the hidden sides drawn in

points.title: ONE PICTURE, FULL 3D
points.sub: Even the sides the camera never saw.

points.claim: The pipeline removes the background, frames the object, and writes a standard 3DGS .ply that opens in any Gaussian splat viewer.
points.spoken: It removes the background, frames the object, and writes a standard PLY file, so it opens in any splat viewer or Blender.
points.source_note: Model card: 'it removes the background, frames the object and generates up to 1,048,576 Gaussians, written as a standard 3DGS .ply' + 'open it in any Gaussian splat viewer'.

visual.intent: photo splits into cut-out, frame, .ply file

points.title: BACKGROUND CUT, PLY OUT
points.sub: Opens in any splat viewer or Blender.

points.claim: It runs on consumer GPUs: 7.2 GB of VRAM, and can run in under 2 seconds.
points.spoken: And it runs on your own graphics card: seven point two gigabytes of VRAM, and under two seconds on a fast card.
points.source_note: Model card: 'It runs on consumer GPUs, using 7.2 GB of VRAM and can run in under 2 seconds.'

visual.intent: a consumer GPU card with the VRAM bar and a 2 s timer

points.title: RUNS ON YOUR GPU

points.claim: You can try it free in the Hugging Face Space, or install the open SDK and call it from Python.
points.spoken: Try it free in the browser demo, or install the SDK and call it from one line of Python.
points.source_note: Model card Demo badge -> huggingface.co/spaces/speridlabs/idol + 'pip install -e .' + 'from idol import IdolPipeline'.

visual.intent: the free Space demo page, then the Python call

points.title: TRY IT FREE
points.sub: The Space demo, or the SDK in Python.

points.claim: On the lab's own benchmark it edges TripoSplat and TRELLIS on every visual column, and it was the number-one trending model on Hugging Face today.
points.spoken: On their own benchmark it edges TripoSplat and TRELLIS on every visual score, and it is the top trending model today.
points.source_note: Benchmark table: Idol bold in SSIM, LPIPS, IoU, DINOv2, CLIP, sharpness distance vs TripoSplat/TRELLIS (PSNR and time go to LGM, footnoted). HF trending #1, score ~765 on 2026-11-08.

visual.intent: benchmark bars with idol's row on top, then a trending badge

points.title: TOP OF THE TABLE TODAY
points.sub: Benchmark: every visual column. Chart: trending #1.

catch: You need an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA for your own runs; two encoder models ask you to accept their terms once; and it is built for single objects, not scenes.
catch_sub: The free Space demo needs no GPU at all.

catch_visual.intent: what to expect: CUDA GPU, accept two encoders once, single objects

cover.visual: a plain product photo on the left, the same object as a spun Gaussian splat on the right

Full-bleed paper with a giant '2s' timer chip, a VRAM bar at 7.2 GB, and a small violet splat object orbiting in the corner.
